abstract: In the late nineteenth through the mid-twentieth centuries, the movement known as Nichirenism sought to realize an ideal Japan based on the Lotus Sutra and the teachings of the medieval Buddhist figure Nichiren (1222– 1282). In pursuing this goal, leaders within the movement sought to mobilize the efforts of women. They formulated a female gender ideology that drew both on Nichiren’s egalitarian reading of the dragon girl episode in the Lotus Sutra and on the contemporary discourse of “good wives, wise mothers” as exemplifying women’s proper social roles. This article has two major aims. One …

title: A Messenger from the Buddha to Modern Japan
abstract: Until recently, the history of Nichiren Buddhism, and modern Japanese Buddhism in general, has focused chiefly on male clerics and intellectuals. This article restores to that history the neglected figure of Matsudaira Toshiko (1890–1985), a prominent female figure within the Nichiren Buddhist tradition. Although famous as a darling of the mass media in the 1920s and 1930s and respected beyond Nichirenist circles as an emerging Buddhist leader and female role model, she is little known today. Matsudaira Toshiko sought to improve the status of women in Japan through a vast array of social …

title: Datsueba the Clothes Snatcher
Scandal in Japan
Found in Transliteration
abstract: This research note examines the complex transliteration practices used by the Jesuits in Japan during the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries, with a particular focus on documents related to the Imjin War, the Japanese invasions of Korea which occurred over the course of 1592-1598. The linguistic diversity of Japanese dialects and the multilingual environment of the Catholic mission in the archipelago resulted in significant variability in the graphical representation of native names in European sources. By analyzing these transliterations, I explore how the Jesuits' policy of …

title: In the Dragon Girl's Footsteps : Women in Nichiren Buddhism and Modern Nichirenist Gender Ideology
Kōmei School and the Path to Compulsory Education for Japan’s Children with Disabilities
abstract: Abstract Kōmei School was the first public school for children with physical disabilities in Japan and emerged from reformist, child-centered influences during the 1920s to early 1930s. This work examines the school’s history to reveal the place of children with disabilities in Japan’s compulsory school system. Administrative exemptions for decades blocked children with disabilities from “compulsory” education, denying them access to school. Kōmei School was established to provide opportunities to a few of many young Japanese individuals with physical challenges and proved to be a source of …

title: Introduction: Performance, Projection, Provocation! Relational Creativity in Contemporary Japan
abstract: Abstract This introduction to the special issue “Performance, Projection, Provocation! Relational Creativity in Contemporary Japan” presents a history of group-based creative practice in Japan, from the amateur endeavors of sākuru (circles) to the professional creativity of international production companies. The special issue applies the concept of “relational creativity” to a series of case studies to better understand how creative practices shape relationships and other social forms, institutional and less institutional.

title: Climate Change and Maritime Security: Challenges and Prospects for Cooperation for the Quad
abstract: Abstract Maritime security is one of the most vulnerable domains to climate change. The Quad comprising India, Japan, Australia, and the U.S., shares concerns of impending climate change-induced maritime security challenges in the Indo-Pacific region. Climate change can catalyse intensified competition for resources and control over sea lanes leading to increased maritime violence. Thus, climate change can derail the collective goals for which the Quad was established – a free, open, prosperous, and inclusive Indo-Pacific region. It is therefore critical for the Quad to understand this …

title: The Fictitious Shine of Japan’s Future
abstract: Abstract Tokyo Governor Koike Yuriko’s vision of a city where everyone can “shine” masks systemic contradictions in Japan’s future-making endeavors. While public proclamations frame Tokyo as inclusive and equitable, actions by Koike’s administration reveal abiding inequities. These efforts align with decades-long projects, most recently manifested in Society 5.0 and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which prioritize market-driven growth while erasing systemic concerns of poverty and homelessness. Ethnographic insights from advocacy groups highlight the necessity of cultivating …

title: What Are the Barriers to Improving the Safeguarding of Children and Young People in Japan’s Entertainment Industries?
abstract: Abstract This Research Note is based on interviews with stakeholders and advocates for child safeguarding in Japan’s entertainment industries conducted by the researchers in Tokyo in July 2024. We argue that, if, as suggested by new legislation, there is an intention to apply UK-style “safeguarding” understandings to prevent reoccurrence of child sexual abuse such as that perpetrated by Johnny Kitagawa in Japan, there are four key barriers to overcome that necessitate increased information-sharing and cooperation between stakeholders in government and industry: precarious work, a reluctance …

title: Japan Needs a Real Right to Silence
Metamorphosis in Motion: Olympic Ceremonies as Sites of Relational Creativity in Japan
abstract: Abstract Examining Olympic opening and closing ceremonies from the perspective of relational creativity, this article analyzes the 1998 Nagano Winter Olympics’ opening ceremony and the 2016 Rio Games’ Japanese closing ceremony—both experimented with transitory meanings exploring alternative representations of Japan. We consider them as cases of relational creativity; the Nagano opening ceremony explored the fusion of local religious traditions and Western influences, while the Rio closing ceremony experimented with meanings of urban cosmopolitanism, consumerism, as well as cultural and social …

title: Relational Creativity in the Aftermath of 3.11: The “Lost Homes” Scale Model Restoration Project
abstract: Abstract Events such the Great East Japan Earthquake or 3.11 force us to rethink our ways of life in relation to nature. Even in the midst of disasters, people have the desire to create and to express themselves—as does nature. How can we understand relational creativity in the aftermath of such disasters, and how might creative works assist recovery processes? This article focusses on the “Lost Homes” Scale Model Restoration Project. The project, initiated and led by architect Osamu Tsukihashi of Kobe University and his students, is a collaborative community project with residents in the …

title: Fighting the Cabal from the Diet: Sanseitō and the Role of Conspiracy as Political Ideology
abstract: Abstract Sanseitō is a fringe Japanese political party founded during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic that has won several seats in the National Diet since 2022. Initially coming to prominence as a promoter of anti-vaccine narratives, the party has since promoted a conspiracist worldview that connects to more conventional right-wing nationalism and addresses a much broader range of issues and beliefs. In this article we outline the core tenets of this worldview and examine how attention to its construction as a participative political ideology sheds light on the party’s …

title: Ishimaru Shinji and the “Populist Playbook”
abstract: Abstract Discussions on populism in Japan have often been overlooked in the comparative politics literature. However, as theoretical and empirical discussions progress, the need for more Japanese contributions to expand observers’ understanding of the global populist phenomenon is evident now more than ever. The sudden rise of Ishimaru Shinji as a populist figure in the 2024 Tokyo gubernatorial election sparked claims that “social media populism” has arrived in Japan. However, although social media certainly played a role in propelling Ishimaru’s popularity during his campaign, limiting …

title: Unfolding the Incidental Process: Nominations Contested in the UNESCO Memory of the World Programme
abstract: Abstract This paper aims to analyze the impact of the Incidental Process activated during the UNESCO Memory of the World (MOW) 2022/23 nomination cycle and the Memory of the World Regional Committee for Asia and the Pacific (MOWCAP) 2021/22 nomination cycle. The Incidental Process is a mechanism that allows a Member State to contest nominations submitted by other Member States in the inscription process of the MOW Register. Japan became the first Member State to initiate the Incidental Process in 2022, contesting five nominations submitted by Korea and China. Japan’s initiative, seemingly …

title: Saving Katoku: A Case Study of the Conflicting Environmental and Economic Demands on Japan’s Island Communities – CORRIGENDUM
Sino-Japanese Children Born of the Second Sino-Japanese War Who “Returned” to Their “Homeland”: Experiences, Identities, and Belonging – ERRATUM
The Okinawan Diaspora in Mainland Japan: Insights from the Hyogo Prefecture Okinawan Association
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the political consciousness, identity, and cultural resilience of Okinawan emigrants to mainland Japan, focusing on the Hyogo Prefecture Okinawan Association. Using surveys and interviews, it highlights how Okinawans navigate migration challenges while preserving their heritage. Key findings reveal a strong affinity for Okinawa among members who were first-generation Okinawan, while younger generations showed a shift toward broader Japanese identification. Cultural practices, such as Okinawan cuisine and traditional events, have remained essential but were …

title: Sino-Japanese Children Born of the Second Sino-Japanese War Who “Returned” to Their “Homeland”: Experiences, Identities, and Belonging
abstract: Abstract This article examines the little-known experiences of children born of Chinese mothers and Japanese fathers who had consensual relationships during and after the Second Sino-Japanese War in China, with a specific focus on those who migrated to Japan after 1972. To understand how and why they—in their own words—“returned” to their “homeland,” this article analyzes historical circumstances as well as Sino-Japanese children’s experiences, identities, and belonging in comparison with other groups of “children born of war” in different historical and geopolitical settings. Their …

title: Tensions and Contestations in VTuber Circles: The “MetaBirthday” Project and/as Self-formation
abstract: Abstract Virtual YouTubers, also known as VTubers, are entertainers who use two-dimensional (2D) or three-dimensional (3D) computer-generated characters to create entertaining virtual content online. This article explores a group project called the “MetaBirthday,” in which VTubers and their followers collaborated to write lyrics, compose music, design stage outfits, and shoot a music video. Through semistructured interviews with the group’s participants and close reading of their published textual material, this article interrogates how VTubers harness virtual and physical spaces to create a …

title: Political Scandal in Japan and the LDP Slush Fund Controversy
abstract: Abstract This paper offers an in-depth analysis of the massive political scandal of 2023–2024, in which dozens of lawmakers from Japan’s ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) received undeclared funds from their factions. First, it provides a detailed timeline of the scandal and places it within the broader historical context of political scandals in Japan. Next, it examines the roles and actions of key participants, including power actors (politicians, secretaries, whistleblowers, prosecutors, and the prime minister) and media actors (mainstream newspapers, tabloid magazines, and political …

title: “CALL4”—Japan’s Public Interest Lawyers Enter the 21st Century
abstract: Abstract This article introduces “CALL4,” a bilingual (Japanese and English) website created in 2019 to bring attention to public interest cases litigated in Japan’s courts. The open-access CALL4 website ( https://www.call4.jp/ ) is designed to both stimulate public interest and raise money for litigation costs through crowdfunding. It presently covers more than 80 cases. CALL4 has become a standard reference for news reporters, lawyers, and others concerned with public interest cases. The site has also raised significant funding. This article profiles the founders and their strategies for …

title: Okinawan Jazz and the Reversion Movement
abstract: Abstract This paper explores the differences between the historical trajectory of jazz in mainland Japan and in Okinawa, where a stronger presence of American military bases monopolized employment for jazz musicians. In the turn of the 70s, while the leftist youth of mainland Japan embraced avant-garde free jazz for its anti-war messages, the economic dependency of Okinawan jazz musicians on American bases divorced the genre from involvement in protests for reversion. Through oral accounts and written records, this essay examines the politics of “Okinawan jazz” and the place of its musicians …

title: The Manchukuo Red Cross Society and the Kwantung Army’s Nation-Building Project in Manchuria, 1938–1945
abstract: Abstract This article situates the Manchukuo Red Cross Society (MRCS) within the historiography of the Kwantung Army’s project to create an independent state in Northeast China, friction with Japanese interest groups already established in Manchuria, and the participation of ordinary Manchurians in state-sponsored organizations. It argues that the Kwantung Army’s sponsorship of a Manchukuo “national” Red Cross society reflected the accelerating pace of the Shinkyō government’s institutional development and pursuit of international recognition as a sovereign state. It also shows that the MRCS …

title: Ririchan the “Grantee Gal”: Post-Feminism, Social Media, and the Celebrification of a Female Fraudster in Neoliberal Japan
abstract: Abstract This research note explores an iconic female fraudster, who achieved celebrity criminal status with a substantial fanbase, by analyzing her status as an empowering female figure and the sociocultural context in contemporary Japan. In due course, we attempt to fill the notable research gap regarding the phenomenon of a female fraudster becoming a “celebrity criminal” from a post-feminist perspective. By analyzing online and interview materials, this article demonstrates that the highlighted otherness in Young’s “transgressive other” (Young 2007, 2011) is hardly applicable. We shed …

title: Trying Haiku Poetry: Collective Creativity in a Haiku Gathering
abstract: Abstract Reading, writing, and literary engagements are often assumed to be solitary practices, but looking at the places where books are sold and discussed, and amateur literature written, reveals the relational side to this creative engagement. This article presents an ethnographic study of haiku composition in Booktown Jimbōchō in Tokyo, Japan, an area known for its literary bookstores, to explore how the social practices of literature unfold. Sketching the social life of a bar in Jimbōchō, I explore collaborative creativity through an ethnographic study of a bi-monthly haiku meeting that …

title: Redeveloping Tokyo’s Meiji Jingu Gaien Area: The Metropolitan Government’s City Planning Runs Amok
abstract: Abstract The landscape of the Meiji Jingu Gaien area of Tokyo is famous; it has a gingko-lined avenue and various sports facilities, including national stadiums and facilities used by ordinary citizens. The large-scale redevelopment of this area has been planned and implemented on the basis of the Tokyo Metropolitan Government’s district plan in 2013 in the wake of Tokyo’s bid to host the 2020 Olympic Games. This paper examines the Tokyo Metropolitan Government’s actions since the formation of this plan, mainly on the basis of the Metropolitan Government’s official documents and Tokyo …

title: Saving Katoku: A Case Study of the Conflicting Environmental and Economic Demands on Japan’s Island Communities
abstract: Abstract Drawing on ethnographic research from Amami Ōshima, southern Japan, this paper documents the ways in which contemporary societies, from the hamlet to the nation state, are wrestling with opposing forces of environmental and economic sustainability and discusses the fractures this creates for people and ecosystems. It uses as a case study the protest to stop the construction of a seawall being built in Katoku, an ocean hamlet in Amami, based within the buffer zone of the island’s United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) World Natural Heritage Site. …

title: Reconsidering the Passage of the 1925 Peace Preservation Law at its Centennial: １００周年に当たっての治安維持法成⽴の再考
abstract: Abstract Based on excerpts from the author’s book, Thought Crime: Ideology and State Power in Interwar Japan (Duke University Press, 2019), this article explores the passage and early implementation of Japan’s infamous prewar law, the Peace Preservation Law (Chianijihō). Enacted in March 1925, this law was utilized to arrest over 70,000 people in the Japanese metropole and tens of thousands more in Japan’s colonial territories until being repealed by order of Allied Occupation authorities in October 1945. Proponents initially explained that the law was to suppress communists and anticolonial …

title: The Heterotopia of Disaster in Post-Fukushima Film
abstract: Abstract This article examines Himizu (2012) by Sono Shion, analyzing the protagonist’s classroom and shanty house as key sites in post-3/11 Japan. Drawing on Foucault’s concept of heterotopia, the study shows how these spaces function as zones where discourses of reconstruction, wa, sontaku, kizuna, and gaman are enforced and contested. While the classroom shifts from ideological apparatus to heterotopia of deviation, the shanty house enables care amid exclusion. Overall, the article advances debates on post-disaster cinema and spatialized trauma.

領と権――近代中国における海洋領有認識の形成

領と権
abstract: 19世紀末から20世紀初頭にかけて、国際法やシーパワーといった、海洋世界との関わり方についての議論や概念が流入することで、中国は海洋を領有するという行為について独自の認識を形成した。本稿は、近代中国における海洋領有認識が、領海と海権という2つの概念の組み合わせから作り出される過程を考察した。 中国は1865年の『万国公法』によって海洋領有の論理を学習し、その結果形成される領域の呼び名として領海という単語を20世紀初頭に獲得した。また中国は、シーパワーの和製漢語である海権を、包括的かつ排他的な海洋管轄を可能とする、ある国家が他国の干渉を排除しながら海に及ぼす力として理解した。張謇や周馥といった清末の実業家・政治家たちは、漁業を題材に領海と海権を組み合わせることで、海洋領有認識の素形を作り出した。陳紹寛や許継祥といった中華民国の海軍軍人は、清末官僚と共通した論理の上に包括的な海洋支配の構想を作り上げたが、他方同時代の国際状況による制約も受けた。 …

title: 北魏の天下秩序に関する一考察
abstract: 近年、中国王朝を中心とする「国際秩序」、あるいは「天下秩序」への関心が高まり、それに関する研究が次々に発表されている。しかし、各王朝・政権の天下秩序の具体的な形態や制度運用、特に北魏という分裂時代の非漢民族政権の状況については、検討する余地が残されている。一方、北魏は常に冊封を通じて近隣諸政権との秩序を構築していた。当時、鴻臚卿が冊封使として派遣される現象は顕著にみられた。そこで、本稿では、鴻臚による冊封を中心に、北魏の天下秩序の具体像を考察した。 鴻臚は九卿の一つであり、伝統的には諸侯と蛮夷の事務を管理する機関として認識されている。北魏になると、兼鴻臚（兼任の鴻臚）を冊封使に務めさせ、王朝の外部に派遣することは常態化し、北魏の天下秩序において、「冊封使を鴻臚とすること」は特殊な意義を持ってきた。ただし、鴻臚によって冊封された政権は、遼西・北涼・仇池・高句麗・宕昌という五政権に限定されていた。授けられた将軍号のレベル・冊封や遣使の回数などから、以上五政権の特異性がうかがえる。そして、北魏はこれらの政権を重要な藩屏としていた。つまり、「鴻臚に冊封される」こと自体が、北魏の天下秩序における近隣政権の重要性を示していた。 …

title: 慶弔外交からみた西国諸氏と室町幕府
abstract: 本稿では、西国諸氏や室町幕府と異国とのかかわりを、弔問や慶賀を目的として行う儀礼的な外交行為＝慶弔外交に注目して考察した。 西国諸氏のなかには慶弔外交を有効に行うものが存在した一方、室町幕府は基本的に慶弔外交を行わないという明確な違いがあった。西国諸氏のなかでは、朝鮮との通交貿易を重要視している対馬宗氏・博多商人・大内氏が、積極的に慶弔外交を展開した。彼らの慶弔外交は、通交統制が進む日朝通交の場で、経済的利益を獲得するための方便であった。一方、日本と琉球との間での慶弔外交は、大内氏と島津氏の行為が目立つが、日朝通交の場で確認できるような露骨な外交交渉術としては用いられていない。 室町幕府は、儀礼的な慶弔外交を基本的に行わなかった。幕府の姿勢の淵源は、中央勢力に浸透する伝統的な外交慣習や対外観による。ただし、日本国王使として朝鮮に渡航した使者が、朝鮮王室の訃報に接した時、進香することで通交貿易の拡充を目論むことがあった。異国通交の最前線にいる境界人のなかには、伝統的対外観よりも、眼前の利益獲得を求める者がいた。 …

title: 満洲事変直前の在満日本人社会と満蒙鉄道問題
abstract: 本稿では、満洲事変直前の満蒙鉄道問題をめぐる満洲現地社会の動向に注目し、在満日本人の鉄道問題に対する認識の変遷と内部の多様な意見を、日本本土及び現地の中国人社会との関わりを視野に入れて検討した。分析の軸としては、在満日本人と満鉄や日本政府という官憲側との関係、及び現地の中国人社会との関係という二点を中心に据えた。 まず、在満日本人と日本官憲側との関係については従来、満洲事変以前の在満日本人が満鉄や日本政府の政策に対して批判的でありながらも、それらに依存せざるを得なかったという矛盾した構図が強調されてきた。これに対し本稿では、在満日本人の満鉄や日本政府への要求や見方が彼らの利害関係や立場によって異なっていたこと、さらに在満日本人と日本官憲側との関係が満蒙問題の緊迫化だけでなく、「幣原失言問題」のような日本本土の出来事にも大きく左右されていたことを明らかにした。 …

title: 地方都市における都市化と市政運営の展開
abstract: 本稿は、1910年代の地方都市における市政運営構造を、福岡県福岡市が同時期に取り組んだ上水道布設事業を事例に分析するものである。 近現代日本社会が経験した都市化は、行政事務の増加をもたらした。これを背景とした1911年の市制全部改正を契機に、都市の政治構造は行政部門が主導する体制へ転換したと把握されてきた。しかし、地方都市を対象とする政治史研究において、同改正の影響を検討した成果は少数である。かかる問題関心の下、本稿は近年「政治資源」という視角から検討が進む上水道布設事業の展開を事例に、市政に関わる都市内外の様々なアクターが関与した市政運営構造の実態を検討した。 その結果として、以下の3点を指摘した。第一に、行政の権能を強化した市制改正に応じた福岡市の市政機構改革では、行政側の原案に比して市会の権能が温存された。加えて、行政事務の専門家も不足し、実態においても市会の「強さ」は際立った。 それゆえ、第二に、福岡市政は市会内の対立からしばしば停滞した。これに対処したのは、市外から対立を調停した筑豊炭坑家であった。その活動は「全市一致」の状況を作り出すなど一定の成果を収めたものの、他方で、都市の「自治」を理由に批判を受け続けるなかで、関与は抑制された。 …

「柳川一件」後、対馬藩の朝鮮外交体制の再構築
abstract: 「柳川一件」という対馬藩のお家騒動は、近世対外関係史にとっても重要な事件であった。対馬の外交僧・規伯玄方はこの事件に巻き込まれて流罪に処された。その代わりに、京都五山の碩学による「以酊庵輪番制」が創出された。通説では、「柳川一件」は、日朝外交における中世から近世への転換とされる。幕府は、以酊庵輪番制を介して、対馬藩と朝鮮との外交の過程に直接介入するという。近年、池内敏氏は、以酊庵輪番僧の職務の実像を検証し、通説を否定した一方で、以酊庵輪番僧と対馬藩の清書役僧・東向寺僧との三者が「相互に有機的な連関を保ちつつ機能を果たした」と指摘している。藤本健太郎氏は、対馬西山寺に伝来した文書を活かして、近世対馬藩の臨済宗かつ清書役僧の総取締役を務めた西山寺の役割に触れていた。これにより、以酊庵輪番制と並行する対馬藩の独自の外交僧体制を見出すことができる。 本稿は、以上の研究動向を踏まえて、従来注目されていない規伯の弟子筋の処遇について考察を行い、「柳川一件」後、対馬藩が引き続き規伯の弟子筋を起用し、朝鮮外交体制を再構築した経緯を明らかにするものである。 第一章では、先行研究を踏まえて、新知見を加えながら、「柳川一件」以前、対馬の外交拠点としての西山寺・以酊庵の歴史を簡単に紹介する。16世紀から17世紀初期まで、臨済宗幻住派僧が外交僧として対馬に起用されていた歴史背景を提示する。 …

title: 大正期東京における演劇検閲の変容
abstract: 本稿では、大正期東京の演劇検閲の変容を、当時の警視庁の演劇検閲に出現した「専門家」検閲官の存在に注目し、その背景にある時代状況の変化、特にデモクラシー状況への警察の対応のあり方などをふまえ検討した。 大正前期、演劇界では脚本の「芸術的価値」に無理解な検閲への批判が高まると、「警察の民衆化」を掲げていた警視庁はそれに応え、一九一八年以降、芸術に見識を有するとされる検閲官を採用、以後演劇検閲官の「専門家」化が進行する。彼らが演劇関係者と検閲をめぐる「交渉」の場を設けたことは、従来の一方的な態度からの転換として期待されたが、社会秩序の維持という検閲の第一目的は堅持され、あくまでその手段として、芸術の理解や「交渉」を行ったという背景から、演劇関係者と異なる価値判断基準で演劇を評価する姿勢に根本的な変化はなかった。 …

title: 越後守護代長尾氏の権力形成過程
abstract: 室町期越後の支配体制をめぐっては、守護代を務めた長尾邦景と、邦景の息子長尾実景の動向が注目される。長尾邦景・実景父子の動向について、かつては室町幕府と直接結びつき、越後守護上杉氏と対立するなかで台頭した、と理解されてきた。一方近年では、こうした守護・守護代を対立的に捉える見方にとらわれない成果も出されつつある。したがって本稿では、室町期における越後守護代長尾氏と室町幕府・越後守護との関係について、全面的に再検討を行い、越後守護代長尾氏の権力形成過程を明らかにすることを目的とした。 本論では、足利義満・義持期、足利義教期、嘉吉の変後の3時期に区分して、越後守護代の変遷を検討した。応永年間後半、守護代長尾邦景は、越後守護上杉氏の動向に伴って上杉氏家中における立場を高めていき、そして応永末年に発生した内乱である越後応永の乱を経て、一国にわたる守護代として活動するようになる。足利義教期には、邦景は越後における守護の職務を幕府から委任されるが、これは越後守護上杉房朝が幼少であった時期において守護の職務を代行する、一時的な措置であった。また、義教期には邦景の息子長尾実景が在京し、幼少の房朝を後見していた。そして嘉吉の変後も、邦景・実景父子は引き続き房朝の下で守護代・守護代代行として、分国支配の中核を担った。 …

title: 明治一〇年代における産業振興の推進
abstract: 本稿では、明治一〇年代における官民の産業振興への志向を考察できる素材として、藤田一郎という人物により全国的に推進された、勧農義社構想の展開を扱った。勧農義社は農業を中心に諸事業への融資を企図していたが、藤田は士族授産のような社会政策的な志向も有しており、事業の安定的な利益への関心は必ずしも強く無かった。そして、明治一〇年代における政府の重要課題は、産業振興や士族授産、或はそれらを通じた民権運動対策であり、勧農義社はこうした課題解決に貢献し得た。藤田は岩倉具視らの熱心な協力の下、一時的とはいえ参議、薩派など政府内の主要な政治勢力からの支持を獲得し、大隈重信や松方正義のような経済政策への影響力が強い高官の協力も得て、勧農義社への政府補助獲得を目指した。しかし、明治一四年には、大隈も巻き込んだ政府内外の政治的対立が激化し、政府補助の獲得には失敗した。官僚との関係では、省創設後から産業政策を主管した農商務省の官僚の協力が注目される。 …

title: 外戚政治から貴族政治へ
abstract: 一般に皇帝と皇后は一対の存在のように思われているが、実は皇后が登場し確立するのは漢代になってからである。近年、その背景には儒学の発展や秦漢時代における皇帝の権威と政治の体制の変質があることが注目されている。しかし、漢代では、皇后の地位は皇帝との君臣関係を示す冊后礼によって確立し、夫婦関係を示す婚姻儀礼がほとんど行われていなかった。皇帝と皇后の婚礼、すなわち納后礼が制度的に確立するのは東晋時代である。このことは皇后をめぐる新たな歴史的展開として重要な意味をもつはずであるが、その意味についてまだ十分な検討がおこなわれていない。そこで本稿では東晋時代における納后礼確立の意味について考える。 東晋で初めて皇帝と皇后の婚礼が行われたのは、成帝咸康二年であった。ただし、その際、礼官の華恒はなお冊后礼を中心とし、婚礼をそれと同じ日に行う「臨軒儀注」と呼ばれている儀礼を定めた。しかし、東晋穆帝升平元年の納后の際、礼官の王彪之は華恒の礼を改革し、婚礼を主体として冊后礼を婚姻六礼の一つである奉迎の数日前に行うことにした。これにより、儒教経典に合致する婚姻六礼と冊后礼を結合した納后礼が実現した。 …

title: 戦国期室町幕府の神祇祈禱と吉田兼倶
abstract: 室町幕府の宗教政策研究の課題とされるのが、幕府と神社の関係である。当該分野は、主として将軍家御師職に研究が集中していた。ところが、近年、唯一神道を大成した吉田兼倶が、文明年間に公武政権の権力核と密接な関係を構築したことが判明した。兼倶と足利将軍家周辺との関係を子細に分析すれば、顕密仏教や禅宗の研究では捉えきれない、幕府と宗教との新たな関係を照射し得ると予想される。そこで本稿では、蓄積のある将軍家御師職研究等を踏まえつつ、戦国期室町幕府の宗教政策に大きな役割を果たしたと予想される、兼倶の活動およびその影響について検討した。 第一章では、義材政権における兼倶の活動、明応の政変への関与とその後に成立した義澄政権での位置づけを考察した。義材政権では、義材の内意を受け願文を起草し、将軍家御師に送付するなど、当該期の幕府神祇祈禱の中枢として活動した。明応の政変時、兼倶は懇意の伊勢貞宗から祈禱を依頼されるなど、義澄政権の成立に宗教面で関与した。加えて、義澄と昵懇の間柄となり、将軍家と唯一神道との関係を一層深化させた。 第二章では、兼倶が作成した義澄の願文、兼倶と将軍家御師らとの交渉等を検討した。兼倶は将軍義澄の信任のもと、祈禱先の選定、報賽内容の決定、願文の文言作成等を担い、祈禱を取り仕切った。 …

戦国期関東・東北地方における臨済宗妙心寺派の動向
abstract: 本稿は戦国期宗教史において研究の進展が求められる禅宗勢力について、戦国期に著しい台頭を見せた臨済宗妙心寺派を事例に、分析の少ない関東・東北地方の動向の実態解明を図った。 まず、寺院分布の流れを網羅した表の作成・分析を通じて、当該地域における妙心寺派の趨勢は駿河経由で十六世紀中期以降を端緒とし、主な活動範囲は禅宗諸派との棲み分けや檀越である武家の影響を受け、東関東・南東北地域であると見通した。 現地で活動する妙心寺派禅僧は、上記の地域的枠組みの影響を受け多様な交流関係を構築し、本稿では修行僧を通じた人脈形成や在来禅宗勢力の動きを見出した。そして、こうした関係の延長線上で寺院が妙心寺派化される事例に注目した。このことは、中央・地方の関係に注目が集まりがちな地方展開史に、地域間同士の関係を併せて読み解く重要性を提起しうる（「地方から地方へ」という論点）。また、禅僧ネットワークとして注目される禅僧間の交流も、修行僧の往来に伴う交流など、住持遷替に伴う移動や住持僧同士の関係と異なる存在を見出し、検討の幅を広げた。また、妙心寺派禅僧の現地での活動は、文筆活動や供養・葬送など個人的結びつきをもとに権威上昇に資する動きが多いことも確認した。 …

title: 草創期の枢密院
abstract: 本稿では、天皇の最高諮問機関である枢密院について、明治21（1888）年の創設から明治23年の枢密院官制改正までの権限や立憲制内での位置づけをめぐる模索の過程を検討し、枢密院が設置された理由を再考すると共に、枢密院がいかなる権限や運用法を有していたかを分析する。 枢密院は明治20年の条約改正問題を契機として、明治10年頃から伊藤が考案していた「枢密官」構想が具体化することで創設され、憲法制定のみならず、閣外からの支持調達や国務大臣の交代の円滑化も目的としていた。しかし明治22年の条約改正問題では不安定要因として作用してしまう結果となった。その後枢密院と内閣の関係が再編され、第一次山県内閣期には、本会議前の事前協議の場として総委員会が多用されるなど、枢密院と内閣との意見調整を図る非公式制度が整備されていく。また議会通過後の議案への適用も想定して、可否のみを議決する審議形態である大体議制度も導入された。第一次山県内閣期の枢密院は枢密院の統制に一定程度成功していたが、枢密院の審議が制限されたことで、枢密顧問官は不満を蓄積していた。 …

title: 第一回普通選挙と仏教界
abstract: 本稿は、一九二八(昭和三)年の第一六回衆議院議員総選挙(以下、第一回普通選挙)とその影響を仏教界に注目して検討することを通して、昭和初期における政治・社会と宗教の関係を提示することを目的とする。 一九二五(大正一四)年にいわゆる「普通選挙法」が成立し、昭和初期から男子普通選挙(以下、普通選挙)が実施されることとなった。普通選挙下では、無産勢力の政治的・社会的動向の活性化や、既成勢力の「自己革新」が見られた。とはいえ、普通選挙が宗教界に与えた影響については研究が進んでいない。普通選挙法は、僧侶など宗教師にも参政権を付与した法律でもあった。そこで、本稿では、宗教界のなかで最も選挙に関与した仏教界の第一回普通選挙前後の動向を検討した。 仏教教団一三宗五六派の連合組織であり、当時、政教問題の活動に努めていた仏教連合会は、仏教界の権威を回復するため、第一回普通選挙で積極的に運動をした。しかし、宗教師の政党加入を禁止した治安警察法第五条第三項が改正されていなかったことと、各仏教教団も仏教連合会や僧侶候補者と距離を置くなど、仏教界全体でまとまった運動ができなかったこともあり、僧侶の当選者は一名のみであった。また、僧侶の選挙への立候補は世間的には異様に見られ、歓迎されない面を有していた。 …

title: イギリス煤煙対策への抵抗と罰金
abstract: 一九世紀イギリスでは煤煙問題の深刻化に伴い、産業の煤煙排出規制が行われた。本稿では規制違反に対する取り締まりがどのように変化したかをヴィクトリア時代半ばに比較的有罪判決数が多かった都市のひとつであるシェフィールドの事例から明らかにする。 一八一八年シェフィールド改良法には煤煙規制が盛り込まれたが、コークス製造に関係するものを除いて訴訟や罰金にはほとんどつながらなかった。その後、新たに規制を導入する動きが一八四〇年代からみられたがこれには根強い反対もあり、紆余曲折の後、一八五四年に煤煙条例が施行された。これには製造業者からの反発もあり、当初は名目的な罰金や対策のための時間が与えられるような判断が多かったが、一八五六年六月以降に初回で一ポンド、二回目で二ポンド、三回目に五ポンドと条例に定められた満額の罰金額が科されるようになったと思われる。しかしその後、有罪判決数は一度低下していく。一八六五年前後には有罪判決数は増加するものの、従業員への比較的低額の罰金が顕著に増加し、また事業者への満額ではない罰金が再び登場しており、初期と比較して事業者への取り締まりは緩んだ面がある。 …

title: 両漢河図洛書考
abstract: 本稿は漢代儒教史研究を推進してきた儒教国教化議論を踏まえ、呪術的な主宰者としての天と理法的・機械的な自然としての天の関係、それによる儒教や緯書の性格、緯書を構成する河洛緯（「河図」「洛書」を書名にもつ緯書）と七経緯（経書名を書名にもつ緯書）の関係を明らかにすることを目的とし、史料の語の内実を吟味しながら、緯書の形成過程を河洛緯や河図洛書を軸に検討した。 後漢の初期と末期に河洛緯や七経緯が受命の書として用いられた背景には、孔子が帝王興亡の期を記録する命紀としての河図洛書を基に命紀としての七経緯を作成したとする緯書説がある。この思想は、天道を人道の根拠とする前漢儒家思想の延長にあり、この流れの中で河図洛書を『周易』や『尚書』に対応させる劉歆の思想や、孔子が天与の図録を基に『春秋』や讖書を作成したとする孔丘秘経説が生じた。聖王の受図伝説を背景に政治権力が古来符瑞であった河図洛書を受命の書として重視し、これを同説が受け入れ、緯書は命紀の体系として形成された。この意味での緯書の基本形は、建武年間の図讖校定から光武帝がこれを天下に宣布するまでの間に完成した。 …

title: 初期緊急勅令の運用と議会政治
abstract: 本稿は、主として初期議会期における緊急勅令（大日本帝国憲法（以下、憲法）第8条）の運用とそれに対峙した議会政治の展開を、同時期の藩閥―政党間対立に即して検討した。 憲政史上初の緊急勅令として発せられた、大津事件（明治24年5月）発生直後の言論統制を目的とする明治24年勅令第46号（以下、勅令46号）は、藩閥政府追及の一大焦点となった。民党の筆頭たる自由党・立憲改進党は、事件発生当時こそ勅令46号発出の必要性を認めたものの、第2・第3議会では一転してそれを否定、不承諾とすることを主張し、かつ責任内閣論などの憲法論を持ち出すことによって勅令発出は第1次松方正義内閣の引責辞職に値するとした。 しかしながら両党の勅令46号不承諾論は、倒閣という政治目標に傾斜する余り合理性を欠く嫌いがあり、特に自由党のそれは、もし松方が首相を辞職すれば党として承諾に転回しうるというほどに権力的動機を孕むものだった。結果、同勅令は第2議会で審議未了となるも、第3議会（衆議院）では圧倒的多数をもって不承諾に決し、第1次松方内閣の信任問題にまで発展した。 …

title: 関東大震災後の帝都復興事業をめぐる政治動向
abstract: 本稿では、大正一二年九月一日に発生した関東大震災後の帝都復興事業計画案の審議過程を、第二次山本内閣をめぐる政治動向から検証する。特に、帝都復興事業を担当した内務大臣後藤新平の動向に注目する。 帝都復興事業は、その計画案を審議する過程で修正を重ね、当初の計画よりも規模を縮小して実施することになった。先行研究では、都市計画に無理解な政治家による後藤に対する政治的な攻撃が縮小の原因とする研究もあれば、後藤の政治的な行動が原因であるとする研究もある。このように、後藤に対する評価が議論の中心となるものの、政治的な要因が影響を与えていたとする点は共通している。 しかしながら、帝都復興事業に関する先行研究において、後藤を含め第二次山本内閣をめぐる政治動向については充分に検証されていない。また、帝都復興研究における基礎的な史料である『後藤新平』は、後藤の伝記という性質上、後藤の行動を肯定的に描写する側面がある。帝都復興事業計画案の縮小の原因を明らかにするためには、当時の政治動向をふまえた検証をする必要がある。 …

満洲国における「主権」の形成と満洲国協和会
abstract: 本稿は、満洲国の国家的性格を、満洲国における主権の形成に留意しながら、解明する。従来、満洲国の性格については、政権と社会との二重構造を前提に解明されてきた。前者を重視すれば、満洲国は日本の「傀儡国家」とみなされ、後者を重視すれば、満洲国は被治者に対して政権の意思や施策を十分に浸透させることができない存在と理解されてきた。本稿はこれに対し、こうした二重構造を前提とする国家像の差異を止揚し、政権と社会とを包括した意味での満洲国の国家的性格を分析し、同国の国家的成長を正面から描写する。 先行研究において、満洲国の主権国家としての欠陥が強調されてきたのは、その建国を主導した関東軍の存在に注目するためである。しかし、満洲国での政府組織や官僚制度が整備され、それを通じての社会統治が日常化するにつれ、関東軍の関与が十分に及ばない行政領域が拡大し、満洲国政府が自立していったとも考えられる。それゆえ、本稿では、関東軍の代行者とみなされていた満洲国協和会に注目し、協和会と満洲国政府との関係性を問うことにより、満洲国の自立性の度合いを考察する。なかでも、満洲国協和会の創立者の一人である山口重次の思想と行動に焦点を当て、満洲国及び協和会をめぐって彼が描いた理想像とその実態との距離を意識しつつ、山口の立場から満州国の性格を照射する。 …

title: 清仏戦争前の清朝外交機関の運営
abstract: 清朝の外交機関のメカニズムでは、総理衙門が南北洋大臣、在外公使、礼部、理藩院とともに、皇帝に直属する対外機関として存在していた。総理衙門は在外公使・北洋大臣李鴻章と隷属関係にないが、三者間の頻繁な連絡のもとで対外交渉が行われていた。このような清朝の外交機関のメカニズムでは、総理衙門と北洋大臣李鴻章や在外公使などのアクターとの協力なくして、外交機関の円滑な運営はありえない。 清朝の外交機関の運営は清仏交渉のあり方と大きく関わっている。清仏戦争前の清仏交渉は、主として総理衙門、北洋大臣李鴻章と駐英仏公使曾紀澤という三つのアクターによって行われていた。本稿は清朝の外交機関のメカニズムとその運営を射程に入れることで、清仏戦争前の清仏交渉（一八八二〜一八八三）を取り上げ、三者間の相互関係ないし意見の対立がどのように清仏交渉に影響を与え、李や曾らの交渉活動がどのように清朝の外交機関のメカニズムに規定されていたのかを検討した。 …

伊勢神宮の中世的変容と祭主・宮司の文書
abstract: 伊勢神宮の古代から中世への変容についての到達点的理解は、11世紀を通じた土地所有制度や神宮組織の変化の結果、祭祀組織の頂点に祭主が位置する体系が形成されるというものである。ところで、命令下達の文書はその発給主体の所持した権力が如何なるものかを直接的に示す素材であり、またそれが具備されていく過程は組織機構の変容に直結する重要な問題であるはずである。しかしながら、これまでの伊勢神宮の古代・中世移行期に関する研究では、11世紀半ばに祭主下文や宮司庁宣など、それまでみられなかった文書が登場することの意味の解明は進まず、その時代移行論上への位置付けもなされないままであった。 …

title: ソ連のシベリアと極東の開発における日本軍捕虜の労働利用
authors: 福地 スヴェトラーナ
abstract: ソ連の対日参戦により満洲で捕虜となり拘束された日本軍将兵について、日本軍の降伏から四日後に発令された国家防衛委員会決定第九八九八号（極秘）により、ソ連領内に移送して労働使用することが命じられた。労働現場への詳細な配分計画が示されたこの決定を、国家防衛員会が日本軍降伏後の極めて早い時期になぜ発令することができたのかについて、本稿はこの決定が一九四二年に多くの開発課題が目標を達成しないまま終了したソ連経済の第三次五ヵ年計画の未達成課題の完遂を目指す動きと密接な関連を持つという仮説を提示して、この仮説を検証することを通じて決定第九八九八号の意図を解釈し、抑留の背景を考察することを課題とする。 第三次五ヵ年計画で目標が未達成となった開発課題に対して、一九四三年から新たな五年間の開発計画草案が作成された。しかしこの草案には目標は示されたものの、労働力については何も示されなかったために、これを実行するためには開発課題ごとに新たに投入する労働力の種類と人数を明示した個別実施命令が必要であった。当初この個別実施命令には労働力としてラーゲリの収容者やドイツ軍の捕虜となり解放された元ソ連軍兵士などの強制労働対象者が指定されていたが、後には労働力が示されないまま発令されたものもあった。 …

title: 地頭設置の政治過程
abstract: 本稿は、地頭設置の政治過程を源頼朝の戦略の次元で跡づける。鍵は、武士狼藉停止と没官措置のふたつである。没官措置と地頭設置の段階差を弁別し、武士狼藉停止をＡ型（特定所領への武士の関与を排除するもの）とＢ型（特定所領における武士の所務を規律するもの）に分ける。結論からいえば、いきすぎた没官措置を解除するのがＡ型の武士狼藉停止であり、両者は反対の関係にある。一方、武士が特定所領内でなんらかの所職を知行することがＢ型の武士狼藉停止の前提であり、地頭設置とは表裏の関係にある。 …

title: 戦国期足利将軍家の地域支配の転換
abstract: 日本の戦国期は、相次ぐ戦乱に伴い、中世的な秩序の崩壊と近世的な秩序の萌芽が見られる移行期である。本稿では、こうした戦国期の地域支配体制の変化を、足利将軍家の御料所支配から考察した。特に、天文十七年（1548）の山城国宇治郡山科七郷の御料所化に注目し、将軍義輝期の御料所支配を取り上げる。 まず、天文十七年の山科七郷御料所化は、足利将軍家と細川晴元・六角定頼の三者による協働という政治的交渉の産物であった。この御料所化によって、中世の複雑な支配関係が一新されて一円的な領域支配が開始し、同時に宗教支配も一新されている。特にその領域は、中世後期に自律的な地域社会を形成してきた惣郷山科七郷の範囲に対応したものであった。よって、将軍義輝期にも大規模な新規御料所が設定されたことが判明した。 次に、御料所経営を分析すると、その代官が室町幕府の財産を管理する公方御倉正実坊と将軍義輝側近の奉公衆であり、御料所山科七郷は足利将軍家の収入源、かつ軍事力を支える財政基盤であった。また、旧領主との関係を見ると、当初は個別的に得分の下行が認可される場合もあったが、徐々に滞り、将軍側近の代官支配が既成事実化していった。つまり、山科七郷は次第に財政基盤としての役割が増していた。御料所山科七郷は将軍家の重要な活動基盤であったため、経営強化が図られていたのである。 …

title: Sam Lebovic. State of Silence: The Espionage Act and the Rise of America’s Secrecy Regime.
abstract: Sam Lebovic has written a timely and important history of the uses and abuses of the Espionage Act. Passed amid the World War I panic about spies and saboteurs, this perhaps deliberately vague law never netted any spies. But with the companion Sedition Act, it produced hundreds of prosecutions for criticism of America’s entry in the war, the draft, and of President Woodrow Wilson. While the Sedition Act disappeared, the Espionage Act lived on to do damage to individual rights and the transparency necessary for democracy. title: Technological Unemployment in the British Industrial Revolution: The Destruction of Hand-Spinning
abstract: Abstract This article analyses the elimination of hand-spinning in Britain during the Industrial Revolution and shows that it produced large-scale technological unemployment. First, it uses new empirical evidence and sources to estimate spinning employment before the innovations of the 1760s and 1770s. The estimates show that spinning employed 8 per cent of the population by about 1770. Next, the article systematically analyses the course, extent and locations of technological unemployment produced by mechanization using more than 200 detailed qualitative sources. abstract: Abstract A recent study, following a subtle but unusual for history of science argumentation method starting from the premises established by stylometry, discovered a drastic stylistic contrast between Copernicus’s early opus Commentariolus and his mature writings. abstract: While a fair amount of research has analyzed the media coverage of refugees in North America and Europe, few studies have looked beyond these common examples in the western context. title: ‘The point is, history sells’: Martin Davies’s political critique of history and heritage
abstract: In this article, we aim to work in the political direction that Martin Davies’s critique of history-focused-behaviour has opened up. abstract: Abstract Bede and other authors describe a destructive wave of plague sweeping across Britain and Ireland in the period 664–87. Here, it is proposed that these developments were influenced by the effects of the plague. abstract: In this article we track the relationship between transforming ways of engaging with animal Otherness in the context of Western scientific writing from the mid-eighteenth through to the early twenty-first century. abstract: Examining the tales of visits inside Cornish mines in the late nineteenth century, this article argues that middle-class representation of miners’ bodies as simultaneously both robust and vulnerable was indebted to encounters with the physical environment. abstract: Abstract In the summer of 1900, at the height of the Boxer War, the European and North American press began to spread the story that all the Western foreigners in Beijing had been massacred. abstract: The employment of mules and the networks supplying them to German Southwest Africa (1884–1915, modern-day Namibia) are at the centre of this article. Mules are infertile and difficult to breed yet of use specifically in disease-prone and arid environments. In German Southwest Africa, Germany’s first and only settler colony, colonists depended on them to cross the Namib Desert, construct infrastructure and fight wars. abstract: In this essay I present the main objectives and the first provisional results of a project on the management of natural resources and the emergence of sustainability problems in the low plain of early modern Lombardy, northern Italy. abstract: Abstract The “Danish cartoons controversy” has often been cast as a paradigm case of the blindness of liberal language ideologies to anything beyond the communication of referential meaning. This article returns to the case from a different angle and draws a different conclusion. Following recent anthropological interest in the way legal speech grounds the force of law, the article takes as its ethnographic object a 2007 ruling by the French Chamber of the Press and of Public Liberties. abstract: Abstract This paper traces discourse and practices among Jewish communal leaders in Western Europe and the United States regarding the need for Jewish missions to China and Ethiopia. abstract: Abstract In Japan, the COVID-19 pandemic unfolded amidst a heated debate about the country’s ‘working style’, work–life balance (or lack thereof), and a growing recognition of the urgent need for comprehensive change in the prevailing work culture. abstract: As commercial tabletop and video games become increasingly popular throughout the world, traditional board games are becoming a form of endangered intangible cultural heritage, and in many places what were once widely played games have largely been abandoned. title: Digital Sankofa: Understanding the Past and Futures of Black Digital Humanities
abstract: In an increasingly digital and digitized world, weaved in algorithms, the meaning and importance of the emerging field of Black digital humanities (Black DH) is central to our understanding of the experiences of Black people. This special issue builds on previous publications to center Black people and Blackness in the current world through the lenses of Black DH, setting the stage for the various meanings and roles Black DH can play in its intersection with others fields and practices that affect Black humanity and experience.

title: Community-Driven Linked Data Approaches in Builders and Defenders: Nashville's Historical Black Civil War Database
abstract: The Builders and Defenders database (www.buildersanddefenders.org) is a collaborative project which collects the biographical information of Nashville's Black population during the Civil War era. title: Library Professionals: Instrumental in Black Digital Humanities
abstract: Librarians and archivists, particularly those whose work focuses on resources pertaining to the Black diaspora, play a vital role in the field of Black digital humanities. Yet, all too often they are left out of conversations surrounding the Black digital humanities. This is a missed opportunity. Reflecting on my own work as a library professional, I argue that bridging the gap between the Black digital humanities and the social sciences, particularly library science, can prove to be incredibly fruitful in all phases of a digital humanity project.

In doing so, he takes seriously the impact of eighteenth-century debates on European political economy on Irish affairs, and crucially how the Irish case informed these wider intellectual debates. Ireland has often been seen as peripheral to the interests of scholars interested in political economy or the Enlightenment—indeed the …

Insects at the Intersection of Gender and Class in the Early Modern Period1
abstract: For millennia, the lives of humans and insects have been intimately connected. Living on bodies, in homes, and in people’s imagination, insects were (and are) an integral part of everyday life. In the historiography of human–animal history, the role of arthropods has recently gained more attention, with historians designating the Early Modern period as a time in which insects were increasingly studied and appreciated. In the domestic sphere, however, insects were seen as unwanted intruders. This essay considers the ways in which Dutch men and women encountered and were expected to deal with …

Demon Slayer Kimetsu no yaiba : Oni, Vampires, and Sexuality
abstract: An oni (demon/ogre) is a fascinating supernatural creature. Depicted in Japanese literature, religion, art, and folklore, the oni’s longevity can be ascribed to their symbiotic evolution alongside Japanese society. The recent Japanese societal phenomenon created by Kimetsu no yaiba, a manga which was then made into anime and a film, reveals how oni still occupy an important position in Japanese culture. Kimetsu no yaiba depicts a war between humans and evil oni. The oni characters in Kimetsu no yaiba across all its iterations possess the fundamental attributes of traditional oni such as …

title: Domain Shinto : Religious Policies, Guiding Ideas, and Historical Development
abstract: This article argues that the restoration of ancient shrines initiated by Tokugawa Yoshinao in the 1630s should be regarded as the starting point of Domain Shinto. It demonstrates that Yoshinao’s constructive Shinto policies were grounded on the same ideology that we find at work in the more famous and primarily destructive Domain Shinto policies of the Kanbun era. The article presents lesser-known examples before and during the Kanbun years that also fit into this ideological pattern. In this period, Shinto and Confucianism were regarded by many political agents as identical and of equal …

title: Domain Shinto in Early Modern Mito : Impacts on Village Populations and Rural Networks
abstract: Tokugawa Mitsukuni’s religious policies in Mito domain during the 1660s are famous for their radical retrenchment of Buddhist institutions but were also designed to promote a system of one shrine per village. As Mitsukuni aimed at a complete separation of Shinto shrines from Buddhism, his reforms can be regarded as a typical case of Domain Shinto. Nevertheless, he could not achieve a comprehensive implementation of his policies. In the village of Noguchi, the subject of this case study, a tutelary shrine had existed since the early ninth century. It was, however, managed by a Buddhist temple. …

title: Salt, Seaweed, and Grief : The Power of Suma-Themed Private Poetry in The Tale of Genji
abstract: In the Heian period, poems in the zōtōka (exchange poem) style strengthened social bonds and supported the court-centered polity, while Buddhist poetry (shakkyōka) was extolled for its religious expression and ability to assist the composer achieve a positive rebirth. Contrary to what is often argued, therefore, private poetry (hare no uta) wielded as much power as public poems (ke no uta). This article will show that these points also apply to fiction of the time. In The Tale of Genji, the “Suma” chapter contains the highest number of poems. All are private and are lauded for the ways they …

title: Domain Shinto in Tokugawa Japan
abstract: This introduction combines an outline of the concept of “Domain Shinto” with a synopsis of the articles that make the Special Section. It centers on the Shinto-related “Kanbun reforms,” that is, policies of an anti-Buddhist character during the 1660s in the three domains of Okayama, Mito, and Aizu. At the same time it makes clear that these are only the best known and most visible examples of Domain Shinto.

title: Trump and China: The Rocky Road Ahead
abstract: Abstract China's consistent message to the U.S. since Donald Trump 's election is the need for deeper cooperation. But Trump and his hawkish advisers and Congressmembers seem bent on a trade war and closer ties to Taiwan. His strategy is that once the Middle East and Ukraine are “solved,” he will be positioned to force Xi Jinping's hand. But the Chinese have options for dealing with U.S. economic pressure. Still, Trump might bargain on U.S. security ties if he can get a deal on trade. The most likely outcome is more tension in U.S.-China relations and a further drift toward Cold War-era …

title: Making Sense of South Korea's Senseless Martial Law Declaration
abstract: Abstract On 3 December 2024, South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol declared martial law, the first time such an order had been given since the country democratized in 1987. Koreans and international observers alike are puzzled as to why Yoon would take such a drastic measure. This article argues that competing visions of the history of South Korea 's military dictatorship era, in which the Korean right views the left as pro-North Korea and the left views the right as Japanese collaborators and an obstacle to democratization, contributed to an atmosphere in which cooperation among the two major …

abstract: A retrospective analysis of the formation of university historical science on the example of the Belarusian State University is presented. The significant contribution of the Belarusian State University scientists to the complex process of institutionalisation of Belarusian historical science is shown. It was emphasised that the formation of history in the republic and the definition of priorities in the organisation of scientific research were largely determined by the needs of the development of the state. It was noted that the most significant collective scientific publications on the …

abstract: Based on a wide range of sources, the stages of institutionalisation of Russian history as a science, directions, forms and methods of its teaching at the Belarusian State University from the beginning of activity of the institution to the 90th anniversary of the foundation of the faculty of history in its structure (2024), are considered. Conclusions are made not only about the undoubted influence of the political component of each stage on these processes, the desire of teachers and students of all generations to improve the efficiency of their work and study, but also about the objective …

title: Johannes Sleidanus: De quatuor summis imperiis libri tres – Die vier Weltreiche. In drei Büchern
abstract: German historian Johannes Sleidanus’s overview of the history of the four empires was the leading textbook on world history for university and grammar school students of the Empire from the mid-sixteenth to early eighteenth century. Alongside the source references provided by Heinrich Meibom the Elder, this edition provides revealing insights into the scope of historiographical knowledge in the Early Modern era.

title: Introduction: Invasive Species, Global Health, and Colonial Legacies
abstract: Bringing together seven papers spanning Southern and Eastern Africa, North America, England, and India, this special issue explores the historically neglected connections between invasive species and health in the long twentieth century. Drawing upon perspectives from medical history, the history of science, environmental history, and environmental as well as medical anthropology, the papers analyze the entanglements of invasive species and zoonotic disease, food security, pesticide, crime, and ecosystem health. This introduction provides an overview of the historiography of invasive species …

title: Translator attribution of Hongloumeng: using entropy-based features and machining learning algorithm
abstract: Abstract This study utilized machine learning algorithms and entropy-based features to identify translators of two English translations of Hongloumeng, a great classical Chinese novel written in the mid-18th century. The translations under examination were completed, respectively, by David Hawkes and the Yangs (Yang Hsien-yi and Gladys Yang). Two feature sets were extracted as input for the identification of translator styles: wordform features (wordform unigrams, bigrams, and trigrams) and part-of-speech (POS) features (POS unigrams, bigrams, and trigrams). Additionally, four machine …

title: Becoming a Bone Buddha: Fragmenting and Remaking Death Rites in Contemporary Japan
abstract: Within a contemporary Japan described as socially atomised and secular, inter-generational Buddhist systems of care for the dead and their remains have become increasingly unstable. In their place, a range of ‘new death’ practices have emerged, from personalised funerals to memorial jewellery and tree burials, but also the unexpected resurrection of a historic mode of communal interment: bone buddhas (kotsubotoke, 骨仏 or 骨佛), which are monumental statues made from thousands of sets of compressed human ash. Drawing on fieldwork with the artisans and communities that design and make kotsubotoke …

title: Relational Plants and Apurinã's Multibeing Life-Making
abstract: Southwestern Amazonia is one of the most biodiverse areas of the world. In this region, plants have a significant place and role in Indigenous peoples’ social relations. They are inseparable actors in human history and crucial social actors within diverse social assemblages. Our article focuses on plant subjectivities in Apurinã ritual encounters, which highlight the elemental role of certain plants in complex relations of various more-than-human and human beings. In the kyynyry and kamatxi rituals of this Arawak-speaking nation living in the Purus River region, the plants are central ritual …

title: Sense and historicity: rethinking history with Martin L. Davies
abstract: This essay examines the unique positioning of Martin L. Davies within contemporary theory and philosophy of history, giving particular attention to the once again timely question of what is meant by historicity and historicization, as well as exploring the ways in which Davies suggests our relation to historical knowledge can, and perhaps should, be reconceived. The examination proceeds in three main parts, lingering on Davies’ relation to ‘postmodern’ theory of history, his all-consuming conception of historical thought and his views on how this sense of ‘history’ might be countered and …

title: CREATIVE DISINTEGRATION: THE PERPETUAL EMERGENCE OF MODERN POLITICAL THOUGHT
abstract: ABSTRACT Michael Sonenscher's After Kant: The Romans, the Germans, and the Moderns in the History of Political Thought offers a rich overview of nineteenth‐century French, Swiss, and German political thought. The work's central argument is that modern political thought emerges in a series of attempts to close germinal “gaps” opened in the fabric of European intellectual life by Kant's philosophy and philosophical history. Less a narrative than a bricolage, the work consists of a myriad of intellectual cameos, walk‐on roles, philosophical speculations, and political and social theories whose …

title: REVISITING MONTAILLOU
abstract: ABSTRACT Based on extensive scholarship in English and French, this article offers an analytical survey of both the laudatory and critical reception of Emmanuel Le Roy Ladurie's Montaillou (1975). I revisit the Latin text of Jacques Fournier's register and compare it with relevant fragments in the French and English translations of Montaillou. This comparison provides a starting point to comment on Le Roy Ladurie's novelistic writing style and the “hypnotic effect of narrative” achieved by the book. It also enables me to address historians’ criticisms of how Le Roy Ladurie used historical …

title: INHERITANCE AND INCEST: TOWARD A LÉVI‐STRAUSSIAN READING OF MONTESQUIEU'S DE L'ESPRIT DES LOIS1
abstract: ABSTRACT The premise of this article is that Montesquieu, while seen as an Enlightenment thinker who contributed centrally to the development of the social sciences before the period of discipline formation in the nineteenth century, is generally appreciated in only the vaguest of terms. To the degree that he has been seen as a social theorist rather than as a belletrist or a political writer, scholars have had to amputate major sections of his masterwork, De l'esprit des lois (1748). In so doing, they have tended to give false or at least only partial readings of a work whose author insisted …

title: MISFITS, POWER, AND HISTORY: RETHINKING ABILITY THROUGH AN ANIMAL LENS
abstract: ABSTRACT In this article, we construct a critical history of “ability” by focusing on the specific case study of dark‐dwelling animals and the ways in which they have been understood over the course of modernity. Such creatures were frequently the subjects of assumptions and judgments about what they could and could not do. Dark places have historically been imagined as extreme environments and as home to equally strange beings. We argue that discourse relating to dark‐dwellers—from bats and hedgehogs to deep‐sea creatures—reveals that ability, in the animal context, relates to several …

title: From parliamentary history to digital and computational history: a NLP-friendly TEI model for historical parliamentary proceedings
abstract: Abstract This article introduces a new method for the digital and computational analysis of historical parliamentary proceedings. The article presents an XML-TEI model specifically designed for encoding historical parliamentary documents; this model is exemplified through the analysis of parliamentary debates from the French Chamber of Deputies (1889–1893). The first part of the article discusses the motivations behind the model’s development. The second part outlines the methodological choices in constructing the model and the need for schema adaptation. We subsequently detail our method for …

title: O‘ZBEKISTONDA TARIX SOHASI RIVOJIDA XOTIN-QIZLAR ISHTIROKI VA O‘RNI (Toshkent shahar davlat OTM misolida)
abstract: In this article, an attempt was made to shed light on the invaluable contribution of women scientists, who are engaged in scientific and pedagogical activities in the field of history, which is considered a field of social and humanitarian sciences, to the development of science in public higher education institutions in Tashkent. History is the great memory of mankind, and it embodies the spirituality, culture, and achievements of our ancestors. A comprehensive analysis of the research, innovation, and experience of historians engaged in such work will shed some light on their remarkable …
journal: Oriental Journal of History Politics and Law

title: Shinran to Marukusu shugi: tōsō, ideorogi, fuhensei (Shinran and Marxism: Struggle, Ideology, Universality)
abstract: Over the past several decades, scholarship on modern Japanese Buddhism has undergone something of a renaissance, with scholars in both Japan and elsewhere reassessing many long-held assumptions (see, e.g. Klautau and Krämer 2021; Ōtani et al. 2023). One fertile area of study is how images of traditional sectarian founders have been renegotiated in different eras of modern Japan, with perhaps none being the subject of as much writing as Shinran, Shin Buddhism’s traditional patriarch. This figure has been reinvented as everything from a national “founding father” and patriotic symbol to radical …

title: Training the Philosopher King: Ancient Models of Political Action in Hannah Arendt and Michel Foucault
abstract: Abstract This article offers a comparative study of Hannah Arendt’s and Michel Foucault’s “returns” to classical antiquity. I focus on their overlapping readings of Socrates as a “civilization trainer” and their divergent readings of Plato – who is for Foucault a trainer of kings and for Arendt a utopian engineer – to argue that both Arendt and Foucault draw from Greek antiquity a substantively underdetermined but politically choice worthy form of action: a courageous and critical relation to the present moment in which one lives, consisting of the public and philosophical critique of what we …
journal: Journal of the Philosophy of History

title: Technology, Modernity, and the Possibility of Historical Understanding
abstract: Abstract This paper traces the meaning of technology in Arendt and Foucault’s work, their historical analyses of technology, and the way that their notions of technology’s role in modernity influence their historical methods. I argue that whilst the two political thinkers approach the idea of technology from different perspectives, there is also substantial overlap in the way that they conceive of technology – often critically – as a wide-ranging set of practices of power interlocked with particular modes of knowledge. This helps to properly situate some aspects of their work that converge, …
journal: Journal of the Philosophy of History

title: Reason to Hope? Arendt, Foucault, and the Escape from Politics into History
abstract: Abstract On many occasions between the early 1950s and her death in 1976, Hannah Arendt argued that modern Western thought exhibited a recurring desire to “escape from politics into history.” What did she mean by this claim, and how valid was it, particularly in her own lifetime? This article explores these questions in two parts. The first part reconstructs her critique of the turn toward “the philosophy of history” in the modern age, and argues that her own project, in contrast, was an attempt to fulfill the hope for what she called “a new political philosophy.” That hope grew especially …
journal: Journal of the Philosophy of History

title: Politics, History, Freedom: Arendt, Foucault and the Politics of Genealogy
abstract: Abstract Arguing that Arendt and Foucault can both be seen as engaged in the practice of genealogy, this article starts by sketching the background figures of Heidegger and Nietzsche that they hold in common and situates their relations to Nietzsche as emerging from dissatisfaction with the lack of historical groundedness in Heidegger’s philosophy. To develop this case and to provide that basis for some comparison between their approaches and diagnoses of the contemporary condition, it then offers an analysis of each of Arendt and Foucault against this Heidegger-Nietzsche background. Finally …
journal: Journal of the Philosophy of History

title: The Politics of Method: Arendt and Foucault on Hobbes
abstract: Abstract In The Origins of Totalitarianism (1951) and the “Society Must Be Defended” lectures (1975–1976), Hannah Arendt and Michel Foucault present unexpected engagements with Thomas Hobbes’ Leviathan. This article contextualizes and elucidates their interpretations of Hobbes by foregrounding the genealogical aspect of their projects. Their readings of Leviathan reflect common methodological commitments and figure the distinct but related problematics which Foucault and Arendt articulate, encapsulating the differences between their influential conceptions of power. The article concludes with …
journal: Journal of the Philosophy of History

title: Hannah Arendt and Michel Foucault on History, Tradition, and Modernity
abstract: Abstract This article interrogates the different ways in which Arendt and Foucault seek to conceptualize tradition in their work. First, it analyses Arendt’s approach, arguing that she put forward three overlapping accounts of the Western tradition – one that criticized the alienating effects of post-seventeenth-century science, one that criticized the Western philosophical tradition as a whole for favouring ‘making’ and ‘contemplation’ over ‘action’, and one that sought to explain the advent of totalitarianism through the stresses that imperialism and racism put upon Western political …
journal: Journal of the Philosophy of History

title: Labor as an Overlooked Entry Point into the Modern Age in the Works of Arendt and Foucault
abstract: Abstract This paper explores Arendt’s and Foucault’s thinking through the lens of the modern labor paradigm. Even if the question of labor is a less prominent path in both thinkers’ research, it leads to the heart of the modern era as they both understand it. In their respective fields, Arendt and Foucault sketch a similar link between the beginning of the modern age and the transformation of the notion of labor. While Arendt directly examines the modern glorification of labor and the emergence of the labor society, Foucault provides numerous analyses of labor as an instrument and target of …
journal: Journal of the Philosophy of History

title: Introduction: the Challenge of Arendt and Foucault on History
journal: Journal of the Philosophy of History

title: A brief supplement to the Two Oldcastles of London
abstract: Abstract My previous investigations of the history play Sir John Oldcastle (Ilsemann, 2017) that were carried out with Rolling Delta and Rolling Classify, are viewed again and supplemented by the results of the General Imposters method and the investigations of Lupić in 2018. The Shakespearean character of the play is also supported by Oldcastle n-grams from Rizvi’s data bank which match Much Ado About Nothing (1598), Julius Caesar (1599), Henry V (1599) and As You Like It (1599).

title: Minoritizing identity: imposing racial and cultural illusions of ‘the Japanese’
abstract: Many identities are originally minoritized products of imposition by majoritized others. Contextualized through the identity of ‘Nihonjin’ (‘a Japanese person’) – one regularly informed by long deconstructed yet still prevalent myths of ‘the Japanese’ (i.e. ‘Nihonjinron’) – I conceptualize minoritization through a three-stage process of imposition, concession, and objectivization. To illustrate this ‘ICO process’ I draw on the experiences of ‘Japanese returnees’ and ‘Japanese biracials’ via in-depth semi-structured interviews. Further supplemented by ethnographic vignettes of those identified …

title: Towards historical news values: Czech news media between past knowledge and current histotainment
abstract: This study deals with journalistic coverage of historical events and their contextualization. It conceptualizes the relationship between history, collective memory, and contemporary media logic. It shows the specific treatment of news values on historical topics and the penetration of entertainment elements into the resulting media content. The case study analyzes the discrepancy between the perceived importance of some historical events in Czech society and their journalistic coverage using the example of Czech media production in the year of round anniversaries in 2018. It utilizes the …

title: A roadmap for the future: Teaching humanities in unexpected places
abstract: Troubling signs about the state of humanities in higher education are not new, but the steady decline in humanities majors is cause for concern. The humanities, however, play a critical role in society and public life, promoting citizenship and public engagement along with valuable skills. There are untapped opportunities for expanding history, and more broadly humanities, appreciation through cross-disciplinary collaborations and stronger connections with pre-professional programs. History of higher education courses in higher education and student affairs (HESA) programs have the potential …
journal: Arts and Humanities in Higher Education

title: Ships, Guns and Money: The Logistics of Revolution and Garibaldi’s Campaign of 1860
abstract: Abstract When Giuseppe Garibaldi set sail for Sicily on the campaign that led to the unification of Italy in 1860, he gave a group of exiled political radicals living in the port city of Genoa the task of procuring weapons, equipment and reinforcements for his expedition. These exiled veterans of the 1848 revolutions quickly developed a fluid yet highly integrated fundraising and procurement organization that provided Garibaldi with the means for success. To do this, they leveraged decades of experience as clandestine transnational organizers, but also relied on the business and professional …

title: The Global and the Earthy
abstract: This chapter is a provocation to think less Globally and in a more Earthy fashion about the makings of History. What will it take to move from the globe as artifice in global history, a taken-for-granted signifier, to what lies beyond that sensibility, the Earth as a fissured, crusted, summited, atmospheric and terraqueous platform? I begin by linking the creation of the globe as cartographic model to the modern definitions of History as a discipline, then move to a discrete bit of Earth, the storied rendition of the fabulous island of Taprobane, in order to think beyond the map and model of …

title: Meat, Livestock and the Colonial Project in 1830s and 1840s Australia: The Frontier, the City and the Colonial Imagination
abstract: From the 1820s, the settler occupation of Australia expanded rapidly, driven by the growth of sheep and cattle grazing. Like similar histories in other settler societies, this story is well-known and has begun to be told in ways that centre the active role played by these animals in both aiding and resisting this colonising project. Yet the ways in which this frontier expansion related back to colonial cities is less widely recognised; pastoral expansion relied on settler cities, and limited export markets meant that beef and mutton glutted the markets in colonial cities. This article reveals …

title: Pan-Asian Decolonization? Iranian Oil, Japanese Tankers, and the Nisshomaru Incident of 1953
abstract: Abstract: This article explores the shared desire for economic emancipation in Iran and Japan and its limitations at the moment of global decolonization, which coincided with Mohammad Mosaddeq’s oil nationalization movement ( 1951–53 ) and Japan’s recovery of sovereignty ( 1952 ). It does so by studying the case of the 1953 Nisshomaru Incident, when the Japanese oil company Idemitsu violated the British-imposed embargo of Iranian oil. Despite Japan’s recent imperial past, the rhetoric of emancipation resonated precisely because of the fresh memory of the Allied occupation of Japan among …

title: THE ADVANCEMENT OF KNOWLEDGE NOW, OR THE HISTORY OF KNOWLEDGE AND THE ELEPHANT IN THE ROOM
abstract: ABSTRACT What role should history play in the advancement of knowledge? Because it was so “hard,” so “unbelievably difficult … to get people to believe” in his Great Renewal, Francis Bacon thought a history of knowledge could provide evidence of advancement—a reason to “believe” and participate in his experiment. By indexing advancement, historians of knowledge could foster it. If Bacon were with us today, he would be happy to hear that the history of knowledge is a thriving enterprise. But upon reading our version, he would be dismayed to discover that advancement is nowhere to be found. …

title: Polynesia against Paris: Indigenous Anti-Nuclear Literature and the French Colonial Origins of Oceanian Reintegration
abstract: Abstract: This essay examines Francophone and Anglophone Indigenous Oceanian literature and art to argue that through the predominantly Polynesian response to French nuclear testing in Te Ao Mā’ohi (French Polynesia), French colonialism has inadvertently generated one key cultural movement toward post-colonial Oceanian reintegration—one that extends well beyond the Francophone Pacific. The essay first examines the prose fiction of Chantal Spitz, Rai a Mai [aka Michou Chaze], and Déwé Gorodé to understand Te Ao Mā’ohi’s (French Polynesia's) and Kanaky’s (New Caledonia's) shared experiences of …

title: Get It in Writing (If You Can): Regulating Foreign Communities in Tokugawa Japan
abstract: Abstract: This article proposes “capitulations” and “contracts” as a framework for reassessing how the Tokugawa shogunate (1603–1868) regulated foreign merchants. Capitulations are an established subject of study in other contexts, but this work brings the concept to bear on early modern Japan. Comparing documents exchanged with the Chinese, Dutch, English, Portuguese, and Spanish communities in the seventeenth century, we find that Tokugawa capitulations changed in form and content. Initial Tokugawa capitulations to the Dutch and other newly arriving foreign communities provided assurances …

title: Globality Without Mobility: Ephemera, 1830s–1860s
abstract: Abstract: Histories of the nineteenth-century world often emphasize movements, connections, and linear paths toward uniformity. It is, however, possible to tell a global history of the nineteenth century that features sessile, globally disconnected actors; scarcely valuable commodities; and convergences that ended. Such is the case with the commercial publishers of late-Tokugawa Japan and the disaster lists they designed before the “opening” of the country in 1868. Disaster lists responded to seismic shifts that were both local and global: the rise of a market for organized knowledge and the …

title: A Late/Post-Imperial Region of Difference: The Ottoman Empire and its Successor Polities in Southeastern Europe, Turkey, and the Arab East, c. 1850s–1940s
abstract: Abstract: This text links the literatures on late/post-Ottoman history and on supranational regions. It argues that the area corresponding to the Ottoman Eurasian provinces before the empire’s step-by-step modern-time contraction became a region in the 1850s–1940s. Two processes pulled this region together: sovereignty contests and state-building impacts between the shrinking empire, nascent post-Ottoman nation-states, and interventionist European empires. While shifting around 1920, the region persisted until these two processes waned in the 1940s. The two processes were entwined. They …

title: The politics of voluntariness in modern history: introduction
abstract: The introduction to the theme issue on the Politics of Voluntariness in Modern History starts by discussing the origins and uses of the liberal discourse on voluntariness in the seventeenth century. It was during this period that philosophers and politicians began to present voluntariness as specific to liberalism. By the same token, voluntariness and authoritarian rule have been declared incompatible. This introduction and the papers in the theme issue critically discuss the exclusive linkage of voluntariness and liberalism – an interpretation that fails to capture authoritarian governing in …

title: SENSORY EXPERIMENTS, SENSORY ORDERS, AND AESTHETIC EDUCATION
abstract: ABSTRACT Erica Fretwell's Sensory Experiments: Psychophysics, Race, and the Aesthetics of Feeling (2020) raises crucial questions about the making of a concept of difference through marshaling the senses to the ends of a sensory order in postbellum United States. In this essay, I argue that Fretwell's book has opened a crucial horizon for rethinking how race and ideas of difference marking gender and disability were remade through the short‐lived but deeply consequential science of psychophysics. While the study focuses on how psychophysics and its aftermaths recast questions of difference in …

title: Two sides of the same coin? Cross-linguistic sentiment comparison and thematic discovery of reader’s reception of Wolf Totem
abstract: Abstract Despite growing attention to the global dissemination of cross-cultural literature, rigorous research on cross-linguistic sentiment analysis remains limited, especially for works like Wolf Totem, which hold both worldwide reach and cultural depth. This study conducted a cross-language sentiment and thematic analysis of online book reviews by Chinese and English readers, utilizing advanced linguistic techniques such as BERT, MAXQDA, and ProtAnt. The analysis reveals that Chinese readers are more critical of the themes “Ethnicity and Culture”, “Society and Politics”, and “Wolf and Wolf …

title: The Significance of Small Things: Small Hydropower in the People’s Republic of China, 1949–1983
abstract: Abstract From less than three dozen in 1949, the number of small hydropower stations in the People’s Republic of China grew to nearly ninety thousand by 1979. By the early 1980s, these stations were distributed across nearly 1,600 of China’s 2,300 counties. In 770 counties, small hydropower was the primary source of rural electricity generation. This article offers a history and assessment of these developments, unsettling our traditional emphasis on large-scale hydroelectricity. The article begins by reconstructing the PRC’s enormous investments in small hydropower from the 1950s to the …
journal: Comparative Studies in Society and History

title: Apprehensive vigilance: Martin L. Davies, philosophy, and the ecological imperative of knowledge
abstract: This essay discusses what I describe as the ecological imperative of knowledge underpinning the work of Martin L. Davies in light of some well-known developments in the history of European philosophy. It also offers some observations that seek to elucidate his view of intellectual life through clarifying his approach to the social and cognitive activities that define it. It ends, in tribute, with some personal recollections of him and his work prompted by his death in late 2021.

title: The Cult of Gay Relics and Queer Medievalism in 1980s Sydney
abstract: Abstract This article explains how the Sisters of Perpetual Indulgence, a group of radical queer nuns, created gay ‘religious relics’ in San Francisco and Sydney, Australia, in the 1980s. The Sisters’ relics are a neglected part of twentieth-century queer history and reflect the role of urban spaces and sexual cultures in the formation of contemporary queer identities. They also represent an early effort to preserve and commemorate queer histories. The Sisters drew on deliberately archaic medieval models to preserve pieces of destroyed sex-on-premises venues and cruising sites that were …

title: The Atmosphere in Spatial History: Digital Evidence and Visual Argument
abstract: Abstract Taking its cue from the weather wars that unfolded around the Alps in the eighteenth century — conflicts between neighbouring towns and polities attempting to divert storms by firing cannons at clouds — this article studies the representation of an environment rarely seen in spatial history: earth’s atmosphere. A survey of maps in different historiographical traditions, climate history foremost, reveals a visual repertoire that is effective for determining the physical properties of weather and climate but detaches the atmosphere from its human and non-human environments. A more …

title: Banking on distant shores: a comparison of the development of foreign banks in pre-World War I China and Japan
abstract: Abstract This article provides the first in-depth systematic comparison of foreign banking in pre-World War I China and Japan. As the article shows, after their entry into China and Japan, the presence and activities of foreign banks in China and Japan differed markedly, with these banks developing a much more prominent position in China. Making use of sources in German, English, Chinese, and Japanese, this article aims to explain why foreign banks in China and Japan developed so differently before World War I. It does so by first providing an overview of the development of foreign banks in …

title: Japan’s Quiet Leadership: Reshaping the Indo-Pacific
abstract: If there is one underlying theme to this dynamic reading by Mireya Solis, it is welcome to a country that has figured out how to do more with less. The book seeks to unravel Japan’s rise, fall, and quiet resurgence. How did a nation that, thirty years ago, captivated the world with its economic juggernaut reputation, come to be seen as a nation in decline, seemingly having lost its drive and purpose? For a time during those lost decades, Solis acknowledges that Japan was deemed the world’s industrialized basket case. However, this is not the book’s main focus. Instead, Japan’s Quiet …

title: Getrennte Wege der Rezeption: Susanne Hornfecks Roman Ina aus China in Taiwan und Festlandchina
abstract: Abstract Hornfeck’s novel “Ina aus China” tells the story of a little girl who is taken from Shanghai to safety in Germany before the Japanese attack on China, and who moves to Taipei after the end of the civil war. Its popularity in Taiwan, Germany, and mainland China differs significantly. While research on Hornfeck’s work has stagnated in mainland China since the publication of translations by Huang Lingxiao and Nelly Ma in 2010, the publisher’s marketing strategy has made Hornfeck famous in Taiwan. Dedicated to the translation and publication of Hornfeck’s novel and its reception in …
